clue.text: Visit taking in South American plant producing oil

indicators.note: the visit word swallows the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
S. Am. abbreviates South American

explanation.surface: A traveller calls on a South American farm growing an oil-yielding crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Its seeds are pressed to give a cooking oil much used in Asian kitchens.

clue.text: Where boat is fitted out with small and stylish attachment to mast

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

a yard is the spar fixed across a mast to carry a sail

explanation.surface: A boat being rigged with a neat little spar on its mast.

clue.text: Dispatch expedition, with children seizing power

explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch and expedition both mean swiftness or promptness in getting something done.

clue.text: Indian doctor China maltreated

clue.text: Change temperature to 500 in metals such as gold and silver

names what the swapped-out letter becomes

D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: 'such as' is the link: gold and silver are the prizes at the Olympics, not the metals the surface suggests.

clue.text: Test learner in gym class, for instance

clue.text: Set of steps — it's between short US politician and our monarch

HM is His or Her Majesty
the 'it' of it's, with the 's (is) as a linking verb

clue.text: What's said, parts of which can be found in overblown announcements

clue.text: Party's method seen in peripheral activity

clue.text: Successful with job application that's put in at the end of the course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having won the post you applied for

definitions.text: that's put in at the end of the course
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the post fixed in the ground at a racecourse finish

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into its two words: winning, the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The marker at a racecourse finish line, and the state of having secured a job.

clue.text: Losing his line would produce rage?

clue.text: Final parts of the essay we had examined

indicators.note: the closing letter of each following word is taken

clue.text: Criminal's illegal activity, or that of many

piracy, whether at sea or of copyright, is illegal

explanation.definitionFit: A plot is an agreement between several people to commit a crime together.

clue.text: Foreboding — tense people gripped by it

clue.text: Held up in pass — took legal action about it

clue.text: Admonish ring-leader for interrupting a head

clue.text: Heavy tool to move slowly — hard, when in prison

clue.text: Create interest in what men, women and children have in common — so English
